claims.text: The untreated RHEA has a relatively coarse-grained microstructure.
The untreated RHEA has limited ductility and localized deformation tendencies.
The untreated RHEA exhibits high strength.
The untreated RHEA exhibits impact-induced energy release.
Adding approximately 3 atomic% Nb with thermomechanical processing will produce a fine, coherent secondary phase along grain boundaries.
The Nb-induced secondary phase will activate dynamic recrystallization.
The Nb-induced secondary phase will facilitate uniform dislocation motion.
Nb atoms will segregate to grain boundaries during high-temperature processing.
Grain-boundary segregation of Nb will catalyze formation of a finely distributed secondary phase.
The finely distributed secondary phase will relieve stress concentrations.
The finely distributed secondary phase will delay crack nucleation during deformation.
Stress relief and delayed crack nucleation will enable more uniform plastic flow.
Approximately 3 atomic% Nb will increase strain to failure relative to the untreated baseline.
Approximately 3 atomic% Nb will produce more uniform deformation than the untreated baseline.
The ductility improvement will occur without more than an approximately 10% reduction in yield or ultimate strength.
The ductility improvement will occur without more than an approximately 10% reduction in impact-induced energy release.
The proposed benefit depends on keeping Nb near a moderate level and obtaining a uniform secondary-phase dispersion.
Excess Nb or processing outside the suitable window may cause over-precipitation or embrittlement and eliminate the ductility benefit.
